raw_response:
Been farming these 13.1 mu for thirty years now, so I've got a rhythm. About 9 mu of the better ground near the well stays in wheat-maize rotation — that's my bread and butter. The other 4.1 mu is sandier, so I keep that in cotton where it does well enough.

**Wheat (already in the ground since last October)**

Now in April I'm mostly managing what's already planted. Before sowing last fall I put down about 40 kg of diammonium phosphate per mu as base plus 8 kg urea, worked in with the rotary tiller. I'll topdress another 15 kg urea at jointing when I irrigate — that's coming up. Total nitrogen works out to around 16 kg N/mu, which is what I've settled on over the years for a target of around 470 kg/mu. Some neighbors push 20 kg and get maybe 30-40 kg more yield, but with fertilizer prices where they are this year the math doesn't work for me. I irrigate three times: jointing, heading, and grain-fill if May stays dry. I'll spray once for aphids and powdery mildew around heading.

**Maize (straight after wheat, mid-June)**

The week after wheat harvest is a sprint. No time for plowing — I use no-till direct seeding with a hired seeder. I'll buy Zhengdan 958 or whatever's fresh at the agro-supply shop, about 2.5 kg seed per mu. Base fertilizer is compound 15-15-15 at 30 kg/mu plus 5 kg urea at planting; topdress another 20 kg urea at big bell stage. Total around 17 kg N/mu. One irrigation at tasseling if July rain is thin, maybe none if the monsoon is good. Spray once for corn borer at whorl stage. Last three years I've averaged about 510 kg/mu.

**Cotton (4.1 mu, transplants go in late April)**

Cotton is where the work is. I raise seedlings in plastic tunnels starting mid-March and transplant around the 25th of April. I use a mid-maturing variety, transplant density about 2,800 plants/mu. Base compound 25 kg/mu plus 8 kg urea, then two topdresses — one at squaring, another at peak flowering — totaling about 14 kg N/mu. Cotton wants more potassium than N for boll set, so I'm careful with that. Two irrigations usually, sometimes three if August is hot. Pesticides are the big cost: regular sprays for aphids, mirids, cotton bollworm, and spider mites — probably five or six passes through the season. I expect around 280 kg/mu of lint.

**Labor and budget**

Seven people in the household but four work off-farm — my two sons in Shijiazhuang, one daughter-in-law in county town doing shop work. That leaves me, my wife, and my older brother who helps on big days. For cotton picking in September I hire three or four people from the village for about 10 days, at around 120 yuan/day. Input cost this year I'm budgeting around 9,500 yuan total. Two of the kids send money back so I'm not scraping, but I don't throw yuan around either.

Reason I keep cotton despite my age is the price recovered last year and I already have the experience and the seedling setup. If lint price drops below 6 yuan/jin at harvest I'll think seriously about going all wheat-maize next year.
